item.title: Lumbar / Pelvic Rotation MET
clinicalUse: Selected non-specific low-back stiffness with muscular guarding
patientPosition: Side-lying or hook-lying according to chosen setup.
stabilization: Stabilize pelvis or thorax so contraction is directed to target movement.
contact: Broad hand contacts over shoulder/pelvis or limb lever depending on technique.
forceDirection: Patient gently contracts into the restricted direction or against the corrective direction while therapist matches force.
mistakes: Using MET in acute radicular flare without checking symptom behavior.
safety: Avoid if contraction/movement is medically contraindicated.
item.visualCue: Barrier → Gentle isometric → Relax → New range → Active movement.

subTechniques.name: Quadratus Lumborum — MET
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve painful side-bending restriction or lumbopelvic guarding when QL involvement is supported by examination.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Side-lying with the treated side uppermost. The trunk and pelvis are positioned to gently lengthen the waist on the treated side without provoking pain.
subTechniques.contact: Stabilize the lower rib cage/trunk with one hand and control the iliac crest/pelvis with the other.
subTechniques.direction: Ask the patient to gently 'hike' the pelvis toward the ribs against resistance. After relaxation, increase the distance between the iliac crest and rib cage only to the new comfortable barrier.
subTechniques.dosage: 3–5 contractions of 5–10 seconds at low-to-moderate effort.
subTechniques.reassess: Lumbar side-bending, standing trunk shift and the functional movement that originally reproduced symptoms.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Pelvic hiking is the key contraction; do not turn it into a forceful lumbar side-bend.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid if the position worsens leg symptoms, produces neurological change or there is concern for fracture/systemic pathology.
